rules: Create known small-data artifacts with dashboard_submit(createTitle, operations), including sources, typed datasets, metrics and components in one native batch. Reports also include set_report_markdown and set_view_mode. No intermediate JSON/Markdown files or scripts are required; file workflows remain optional.

If data needs importing before composition, use dashboard_create for an empty container, then dataset_import, dataset_attach or query_execute with its revision. Data write receipts include dataset fields, sourceId, metric definitions keyed by ID and nextCalls for dataset_preview/dashboard_get. Follow current receipts rather than guessing revisions or metric IDs.

contains filters accept zero or one text value, match a declared string field without case sensitivity, and update only explicit componentIds. Local filtering queries the immutable data version; it never reruns the upstream source query.

Read dashboard_get before editing and supply its document.revision as expectedRevision. Within a batch, use the revision from each successful write; MCP summaries return it at the top level. Read again when actual content is needed or a conflict occurs.

Project edits follow dashboard_get -> dashboard_submit(expectedRevision, operations) -> dashboard_preview once. Omit operations to check and save a reviewed imported or restored draft. Preview reads the latest completed checkpoint.

DOCTOR_FAILED means the changed draft remains but no checkpoint was created. Read the issues and submit corrections against the current revision. REVISION_CONFLICT requires reading and reconciling current content before retrying; never replay an uncertain write blindly.

Save with dashboard_submit. Set a specific saved revision as the formal publication with dashboard_publish(revision). Create a visitor link with dashboard_share_publish(revision, requestId) only when requested. Sharing preserves the draft, saved history and formal publication. Retry an uncertain share with the same arguments and requestId.

Checkpoint published is a retention-protection marker. A visitor link is an independent copy with its own access key and expiration. Manage existing shares in the editor. Static-site export returns a ZIP for separate deployment.

Use dashboard_annotations to read saved review comments, quoted text, relative selection rectangles and target identities without chart datasets. It returns the current revision and raw annotations separately from derived targets. Missing components have componentExists=false; text/area anchors need rendered-page verification when ambiguous.

When the user requests changes based on annotations, read canonical content with dashboard_get and modify the corresponding component, metadata or report Markdown through dashboard_submit. Preserve annotations unless the user asks to edit/delete them via dashboard_annotations_update.
Every operation object must include its op name.

Operations are atomic. References are checked after the entire batch. Invalid initial operations are rejected before creating the new container; a later DOCTOR_FAILED retains the changed draft for correction.

Dataset metadata lives in manifest.datasets. Stored rows live in immutable local data versions referenced by snapshot.datasetRefs; bounded legacy snapshots may use snapshot.datasets instead. Never store both for the same dataset.

MCP defaults to local mode: computed contains chart aggregates and the current table page, never the full observation table. Reader filters, sorting and pagination use dashboard_view without saving a revision.

dataset_preview reads a dataset before components exist: dashboardId/datasetId, optional expectedRevision/dataVersion, offset=0 and limit=20 (maximum 100). It returns fields, sourceId, totalRows and bounded rows without component filters. Samples do not establish full-data distributions or distinct counts; component_data provides an existing component's filtered rows.

dataset_import accepts exactly one of rows or csvText and optional fields. Empty rows require explicit fields. Inferred numeric sum metrics remain unverified; confirm grain, units and aggregation before binding them. A string identifier must not become a business sum.

Use dataset_attach with an operator-configured read-only SQLite alias to import full data in a stream. Share one dataset and metric definitions across KPI, chart and table bindings; do not expand simulated dimensions or persist duplicate display rows.
Use dataset_export for all matching CSV rows. Offline component artifacts with remotePage are explicitly current-page snapshots; they cannot paginate or export full local data.

Configuration history and data versions are independent. dashboard_migrate creates a managed backup; dashboard_migration_rollback restores it as a new revision. Layout/title edits retain data references.
Metric aggregation=ratio requires numerator and denominator numeric fields; sum(numerator)/sum(denominator), never avg(ratios).
format=percent requires scale=fraction. Raw 0.98 displays as 98%.

All breakpoints must place each component exactly once; placement is automatically added for new components: KPIs join a trailing KPI row, charts pair two per desktop row, tables and text span the width.
Layout templates are optional starting points. Use set_layout for business-specific composition at every breakpoint.
In filtered-report, filters with scope=table target exactly one table and appear above it; other filters appear at the report top. Conditions combine.
manifest.viewMode is optional and defaults to dashboard; report mode does not change dashboard layouts.
manifest.report.markdown is canonical source (0-200000 characters). Ordinary Markdown prose and chart fences determine the report, independently of dashboard layouts.

A top-level fenced code block with exact info string chart must contain one JSON object with required componentId and optional plain-string caption (0-500 characters) and source (0-1000 characters). The ID must resolve to an existing non-text chart, KPI, table or original component after the atomic batch. Existing componentId-only fences and repeated references are allowed.

Figures are numbered in source order by the report renderer. Standard Markdown links such as [图](#fig-trend) refer to the first figure for component trend and display its figure number. No separate figureId is stored.

KPI descriptions are not allowed in put_component, including subtitle, description, desc, note, detail, rankSub, trendLabel and gaugeSub. Historical prose is hidden; metric definitions remain available in details.

KPI yoy/mom comparisons accept finite numeric values or signed display text. Nonzero unsigned text is rejected; preserve actual direction, units and precision when binding metrics. Zero and missing values stay neutral.

Synthetic prototypes should use the smallest representative dataset covering required filters and states, reused across charts and tables. Do not duplicate calculation/display rows or silently sample real business data. Successful JSON serialization alone does not verify the preview.

MCP text content and structuredContent carry the same complete JSON or transport envelope. Read structuredContent.document when inline. When transport.resourceUri is present, read that exact MCP resource for the complete JSON, preserving encoded project routing. Do not treat the envelope as the artifact. Chunk assembly is a client protocol; hosts with resource-size limits can use the complete configuration download client.

Chart fences accept backticks or tildes, at least three characters, with up to three leading spaces; the closing fence uses the same character and at least the opening length. Unclosed chart fences, invalid JSON, duplicate JSON keys, unknown fields and missing/text references cannot be persisted. Other code blocks are inert text.
set_report_markdown replaces canonical source without changing view mode, components, data or dashboard layouts. Existing legacy subtitle/blocks are retained as inert history.
set_view_mode=report initializes missing Markdown from the title, legacy subtitle/blocks or desktop reading order (y, then x), escaping legacy plain text. Existing Markdown survives view switching.

Legacy set_report still replaces report metadata; old subtitle (0-1000 characters) and blocks (at most 100 unique block IDs and component references) remain supported when Markdown is absent. IDs use the existing 1-80 character rules.

New components never append to canonical Markdown. remove_component rejects deletion while a chart fence still refers to the component; first remove that fence with set_report_markdown. Legacy-only block reports retain their old append/delete behavior.

Local MCP projectRoot selects an absolute project asset directory; remote MCP selects a project inside its workspace. Data connections are operator-configured aliases and exports use managed IDs; tools do not accept arbitrary data/export file paths. Obtain allowed aliases and source schema from project context or the operator; MCP does not discover or configure connections, and missing access is not resolved by generating a script.

Legacy put_component uses kind=legacy plus explicit family and config: chart uses code/data/presentation, KPI uses type/label/explicit values (mc03 needs sparkData or sparkline), table uses columns/rows. These fields are conditional, not required together.
charts://declarations provides required-field schemas and original family/code requirements with authoritative validator sources and coverage limits.

The original discovery catalog lists chart, KPI and table entries; its installed validator registry has 40 chart codes and 16 KPI types (mc01-mc16). Do not use every catalog entry as a chart code. Choose KPI shapes by question (chart_declarations returns kpiGuide), not mc01 for every metric.

Preset charts require registered code/data/presentation. Custom charts use renderer=echarts or html with any non-empty code and explicit content. Unknown preset codes fail before saving with an actionable renderer error.

config.echarts supports arbitrary native JSON options. renderer=html supports executable JavaScript and compiled React in an isolated frame. Custom renderers currently use explicit data snapshots, not preset dataset bindings. See docs/implementation/echarts-options.md.
Source verification supplied is not proof of execution or certification.
